description:
The delivery path, read where ADR-0098 put it: in the plan's `## Contract` block. `/acs:create-impl-plan` judges the path ONCE, from the plan's own scope, and writes it into the plan; `acs plan path` (plan-approval.py path) is the read every later step makes — `/acs:code` dispatches to its leg from `delivery_path`, and the four always-run steps read `owes` to decide whether they owe anything.

This group succeeds the five retired `acs path show | set` cases. That surface judged and STORED the path on `pipeline-state.json`, so its cases were mostly about the write — refusing an undeclared path, an unexplained one, and a re-judge. Under ADR-0098 there is no write: the judgement is the plan, and the refusals that survive are refusals to ACT on a contract that cannot be acted on. The case that matters most is the pair PLAN-PATH-001 / PLAN-PATH-003, which is what makes `delivery_path: null` readable: a plan that has not been judged is not the same thing as a plan whose Contract block does not parse, and a caller that cannot tell them apart will dispatch on a typo.

Profile: run = one open run (TKT-1) over the ticket the path is judged for. The plan is seeded under `runs/<run-id>/steps/create-impl-plan/`, which is where the script resolves it and nowhere else.

cases.title: a plan with no Contract block reports no path, rather than guessing one
cases.note: ADR-0098: the path is judged once by /acs:create-impl-plan and recorded in the plan. A plan that carries no `## Contract` has not been judged, and saying so is the answer — an unclassified plan is a plan that is not ready to dispatch. `contract_errors` is empty because an absent block is a plan written before the judgement, not a broken one.

files.text:
# Add user login

The plan, written for a human to approve in one read. It names the files
and the tests, and it stops there: nothing below is machine-readable yet.

cases.title: a judged plan prints its path back with the owes flags decided alongside it, and writes nothing
cases.note: ADR-0098 moved BOTH machine-readable answers into the plan: the delivery path /acs:code dispatches on, and the `owes` flags that replaced the workflow's `when:` predicates. The reason that decided the path is recorded beside them, in the plan itself, which is the artifact the PR reviews — under the retired `acs path set` it lived on pipeline-state.json, away from the evidence. `after` pins the other half of the contract: `path` is a READ, so it leaves no plan-approval.json behind (ADR-0097 keys that record to the run).

# Add user login

Prose a human approves in one read.

## Contract
delivery_path: standard
owes:
  api_contract: true
  test_cases:   true
  e2e:          false
  reason: "CLI-only change; no HTTP surface, no browser flow"

### Executor tasks & file map
- task 1: src/acs/hooks/scripts/acs_lib/run.py, tests/acs/test_run.py

cases.title: a Contract the dispatcher cannot act on is refused a path, and says of each clause why
cases.note: ADR-0098: `/acs:code` dispatches to `code-<path>`, so a path outside the declared vocabulary has no leg to dispatch to and must not be passed on as if it had one. The path is withheld — `delivery_path: null`, the same value PLAN-PATH-001 gets — and `contract_errors` is what tells the two apart: absent there, and here naming every clause that cannot be acted on, including an `owes` flag that is not a boolean and one that is not an owes key at all. Recorded as a list of needles, not the bare string its predecessor asserted nothing with.

owes.test_cases: expected true or false, got 'maybe'
owes.nonsense: not one of api_contract, test_cases, e2e

cases.title: a --plan pointing outside the plan step is refused before anything is read
cases.note: ADR-0098 made the plan the record of the judgement, so a contract printed for this run must come from THIS run's plan: an escaping `--plan` would report a path that belongs to no run, and a caller cannot see from the JSON which bytes it was read from. The refusal is silent on stdout — a guard that still printed the contract it refused to read would leak exactly what it was guarding.

cases.title: `acs plan path` reaches the same read through acs.py, and is still a read
cases.note: REDESIGN-IMPLEMENTATION-PIPELINE.md:1099 records the replacement by its consumer-facing spelling: `acs plan path` replaces `acs path` (MAR-521, §4.8). acs.py forwards a delegated verb VERBATIM except for `plan check`, whose verb it drops — so the one way this seam can break is `path` being dropped too, which would silently turn ADR-0098's read into the approval WRITE. `after` is what catches that: `check` leaves a state.json in the step, and `path` leaves the step empty but for the plan it read.
